transcript.text: How is everybody doing? Welcome back to another Dragon Wilds video. Guys, we just got a massive update for Dragon
Wilds. This is the 1.0.1 update. As you guys know, for these videos I go over the most important changes and then I
will go over some other ones that are pretty significant and then I will have every bug fix and change up on screen
for you to view. Some of the biggest things that came out of this are save fixes. Developers have implemented a
range of fixes targeting the disappearing world saves as well as introduced a catch-up mechanic for
corrupted character saves that will let you drop in with a fresh character with aggregated stats and tier four gear to
get you back into the fight. Now, the developers do say that they are aware there may still be the occasional player
affected by other instances of save issues that they're still collecting data on and working towards improving.
So, the majority of these save corruption problems have been fixed, but they are letting us know that there may
be some present in the game that they're still investigating. They do say that the problems are very, very small. They
are affecting a small number of players, but it matters all the same to them. Now, the core improvements with the
1.0.1 update are mainly to things like combat, the range skill, as well as introducing new things to farming, UI,
menu sorting, as well as gear. First up, they're introducing the jump attack. On
unlocking the skill tree perk death from above, anytime you are slightly above the max height of the double jump arc
from the ground, inputting an attack will plunge you downward to slam into enemies below. Now, damage does scale
with the weapon you do currently have equipped, so make sure you're holding something hefty before you leap. A wind
step does work with this as well, so you can activate wind step and still use this jump attack. Height does not
dictate damage, like I said, damage is completely dependent on what weapon you currently have equipped. Now, range had
a wide variety of changes done to it and I'm going to tell you guys right now, range is in a pretty good spot. It feels
very good. You have a lot more movement and a lot more options with range across the board. They added a ranged skill
perk, which is ammo recovery, and its greater version later in the skill track. This allows a chance to recover
arrows from bodies of slain enemies. Ranged weapon sub classes are receiving their own special attack variants to
make them feel more aligned with the fantasy of using the short bow, long bow, as well as crossbows. Short bow now
has a special attack called rapid fire, where you hop backwards and fire off three arrows in quick succession, and
you can switch between targets during this attack, which is great, allowing you to spread damage across multiple
enemies. Long bows now have a new skill called power shot, which your character takes a knee to draw an arrow at full
strength. This allows you to let fly a staggering, enormously powerful shot at great distances. So, not only is the
damage of this special attack extremely high, but it can also go great distances. This attack is super fun to
use. It's very awesome, and it does a massive amount of damage. Crossbows also now have a special attack called heavy
bolt, where your character racks a bolt and you let it fly after a short charge. This as well hits for massive amount of
damage and applies enchanted effects on hit. A new perk has been added as well called low blow, which allows ranged
attacks that hit an enemy in the legs or the lower third part of their body will allow you to apply a debuff called
hamstring. This reduces enemy movement speed for a short time. Keep in mind this can't be used with tiny or colossal
enemies. No world bosses, no chin chompas, anything in between, you will be allowed to apply this debuff. This is
great because if you main ranged and multiple enemies are after you, you can shoot them in the leg and you can
stagger them and apply the hamstring debuff to them, and they will kind of de-aggro you for a little bit. This is
really good if you couple it with the short bow's rapid fire, as it shoots off three arrows in rapid succession. You
can switch targets mid-skill, allowing you to apply this debuff really quickly to multiple enemies. And rune arrows and
bolts now do more damage than adamant is now at 4.9 times damage versus the 4.2 times that it was at previously. On top
of this, which was very interesting to me, I did not think that this necessarily was needed, but it's very
welcomed. The inventory space has been increased from 32 to 40 slots, which is pretty awesome. They improved inventory
and chest sorting and functionality across the board. Inventory sort now functions by weight, type, as well as
latest collected. Weight is the cumulative stack weight and heaviest first, type are categories of items
alphabetically, and latest is the most recent picked up item first. They also added a dedicated ring and amulet slot.
This is huge, so now we can use XP rings to get that XP bonus as well as having an amulet to have a bonus effect or
damage increase. Very, very welcome changes. This is just going to assist us in building our character the way we
want, and this is very, very awesome. Now, the amulet of glory was providing additional bonuses above what it was
initially intended. So, they're dropping those numbers back down to better align with what they wanted it to be at. So,
keep in mind, amulet of glory is still good. The scaling of it has just been reduced. They've also added the ultra
compost bin because the super one just wasn't cutting it, and they added the large compost bucket, which has a larger
capacity, which is absolutely amazing. The large compost bucket basically doubles in capacity going from 150 to
300. This is a very, very welcome change, especially for farming. They also added a completed quest tab
including a short summary of the outcome of the quest. This is really good. Just
cleaned up the UI, guys. Now, we can see what quests are active, what quests have
been completed. I really like this. This is something I've been wanting all throughout early access. Happy to see
this come to the game. They also added a toggle for the visceral attack camera, so if you do not like that attack
camera, you can turn it off in the menus under gameplay. They fixed an issue where users on mounts could not open the
map correctly. That's awesome. Obstacles and enemies now respawn in the scorn Wilderness raid on reset and next
run-throughs. Overdrive can now be cast on the advanced spinning wheel. Big one, guys, is the fishing cape now correctly
displays the skill cape perk. So, you have a small chance to instantly catch a fish while wearing this cape. They
removed the ability to rebind certain keys for settings that could soft lock the player in certain instances, like
interact, remove spell, building, cancel building, quick interaction, crafting tab left and right, quest dialogue,
continue conversation, cancel conversation, and select answers 1, 2, 3, and 4. So, guys, right there alone,
those are some massive changes to the game. Range feels very fleshed out and very good. If you haven't been enjoying
it, or you've been enjoying it, I recommend you checking it out because it is now in a very, very good position.
And I honestly want to switch to range on one of my characters and just test it out as my main combat style. Other big
changes I want to go over is players who obtain quest items early through multiplayer or their own server can now
progress to new regions. Properly, this is good. This now has been fixed. So, if you get an item early before starting a
quest line, you can still progress that quest. They fixed circumstances where Coldra would not drop ascension cores.
They fixed artisan and construction cape perks not activating when repairing or building. They fixed an issue where HP
sometimes was failing to regenerate when consuming a food. Enfeeble now reduces damage across all enemy types, and they
fixed certain enemies not being affected by the enchanted bolt effect. They also reduced enemy spawn timers. So, if
you're in an area for too long after taking out guys, you will not have to worry about them respawning. As well as
enemy aggro distances have been reduced as well because as you guys know, you're running around the world and you have a
group of enemies basically training behind you, aggroing you. The distance in order to get enemies to aggro you has
been increased. Other huge fixes is UI scaling is now available across all platforms as intended. They fixed mouse
navigation failing on the skills menu the first time it was opened during a session, inconsistent inventory tooltips
on Xbox and PC, resolved the missing chest sort button indicator on console, they fixed controller navigation
problems in chest inventories, fixed consumables causing a permanent item cool down overlay, incorrect image
scaling inside the journal, that was a huge thing that I did not like, the images would just get blown out. Now
guys, there is plenty of other changes in this update. This is a pretty good update in my opinion, a lot of it is bug
fixes. That is what I like to see. I want them to iron out this game before introducing too much. I'm very happy to
see that they are fixing a plethora of problems that the game has had across PC and console. We do like to see that. I'm
also very surprised, like I said, about the inventory increase, as well as the amulet and ring slot being added. I did
not think that these were coming to the game, at least at this point in this early, but those are very welcome
changes. So let me know what you guys think about this update. What's pretty interesting is I thought we were going
to get some new quests and new activities for the game. That's kind of like what they were talking about with
RuneFest with the October update, but it seems like they are pushing that back and deciding to push that back to
address range as well as all these quality of life fixes, and I honestly welcome that. Like I said, I would
rather them iron out this game and get it flushed out, get it working properly across PC and console before introducing
anything else. It seems we're going to be getting the new quest line, new activities, as well as more quality of
life features coming early in November, and then we have Luminance in December. Go test out range, guys. It's absolutely
amazing. If you guys enjoyed this video, drop a like on it and subscribe for all things Dragon Ball Z. That's what we do
here. We're on the road to 30,000 subscribers. We'd love to have you, and as always, guys, stay happy, stay hyped,
and have a beautiful day.
